title: Publishing 'Yacht Club Swing' and Fats adding his name
summary: Jack Bregman published his tune in 1938; Fats put his name on it to help sales, and Autrey got a few dollars but not what he should have.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well, now, you're saying things that sort of reflect a little bit on Kirkeby. Really -- actually, what did he do? Was it just a personality problem? Or --

Well, I really -- maybe I shouldn't say the things I have said, because I don't have the proof. I was -- it was hearsay by some very important people. For instance, Bergaman? You remember him? Mr. Bergaman? Jack Bergaman? He's a publisher, vocal --
Bregman Voces and on Kahn, yeah.

Well he's the one who published my tune, 'Yacht Club Swing?' And I have a copy here somewhere. Anyway, Fats -- I did it while Fats was in Europe, and he too -- Fats came back, he put his name on there to help --

Yeah. To help -- so to help -- in 1938, help the sale of it. And it went like hotcakes. They were using it like a theme from New York to the coast and back, and all that. I got a few dollars out of it, but not what I should have.
Anyway, that's another story. Which we should put -- I should put in my book.
MR. WILSON: We'll get to that in a minute.
